# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Overview

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto, titled "For a Fair Deal," presents a comprehensive vision for addressing what they characterise as Britain's broken systems under Conservative governance. Party leader Ed Davey argues the election represents an opportunity to transform British politics and deliver genuine change for struggling families and communities.

## Core Themes

The manifesto centres on five key themes: economic fairness, improved public services, environmental protection, international cooperation, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party pledges responsible fiscal management while investing in green infrastructure and renewable energy. Key commitments include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy to support high streets, expanding apprenticeships through reformed training levies, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. They promise to repair relations with Europe, arguing the Conservative Brexit deal has damaged trade and economic growth.

## Healthcare and Social Care

The NHS receives substantial attention, with promises to guarantee GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) and recruit 8,000 additional GPs. The party commits to ensuring NHS dental access for emergency care, boosting cancer survival rates with treatment starting within 62 days of urgent referral, and placing mental health professionals in every school. Free personal care would be introduced, modelled on the Scottish system, alongside establishing a Royal College of Care Workers and increasing carers' minimum wage by £2 hourly.

## Environment

Environmental policy features prominently, with commitments to achieve net-zero emissions by 2045. The manifesto promises 90% renewable electricity generation by 2030, an emergency home insulation programme, and a rooftop solar revolution. Addressing the sewage scandal, they would transform water companies into public benefit organisations, ban executive bonuses until pollution ends, and replace Ofwat with a stronger regulator.

## Housing

Housing commitments include building 380,000 homes annually, with 150,000 social homes. They would ban no-fault evictions, create a landlord register, abolish residential leaseholds, and end rough sleeping within the Parliament.

## Education

Education proposals include free school meals for all children in poverty, a tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils, increased school funding above inflation, reinstating maintenance grants for students, and dedicating mental health professionals to every school.

## Immigration and Democracy

On immigration, the party would scrap the Rwanda scheme, provide safe legal routes for refugees, and lift the ban on asylum seekers working after three months. Democratic reforms include introducing proportional representation, votes at 16, and capping political donations.

## International Affairs

Internationally, the Liberal Democrats would increase defence spending toward 2.5% of GDP, reverse army cuts, maintain NATO commitment, and follow a four-stage roadmap to rebuild EU relations, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership.
